thc.name: THC (Cannabis)
thc.what: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main psychoactive component of cannabis. Urine tests detect its metabolite (Δ9-THC-COOH), which persists after use.
thc.significance: THC is the most common drug screened in workplace testing; cut-off typically 50 ng/mL.
thc.interpretation: Positive = THC metabolite (Δ9-THC-COOH) detected above cut-off (presumptive). Negative = below cut-off.
thc.limitations: Presumptive result — confirm positives by GC-MS/LC-MS. Passively-exposed individuals may rarely screen positive.

faq.a: Typically 50 ng/mL for workplace urine screening, aligned with SAMHSA-style thresholds.

references: SAMHSA. Mandatory guidelines for federal workplace drug testing programs.

cocaine.name: Cocaine (Benzoylecgonine)
cocaine.what: Cocaine is a stimulant; urine tests detect benzoylecgonine, its primary metabolite.
cocaine.significance: Cocaine is a standard panel analyte in workplace and clinical drug screening (cut-offs 100–300 ng/mL).

amphetamine.name: Amphetamine
amphetamine.what: Amphetamine is a central-nervous-system stimulant (also prescribed for ADHD/narcolepsy).
amphetamine.significance: Screened in workplace panels; confirmatory testing distinguishes prescription use from misuse.
amphetamine.limitations: Cross-reactivity with some sympathomimetics; confirm positives.

methamphetamine.name: Methamphetamine
methamphetamine.what: Methamphetamine is a potent illicit stimulant (crystal meth).
methamphetamine.significance: A standard workplace-screening analyte; cut-off 1000 ng/mL.
methamphetamine.interpretation: Positive = methamphetamine detected (presumptive). Negative = below cut-off.
methamphetamine.limitations: Cross-reactivity with some sympathomimetics possible; confirm positives by GC-MS/LC-MS.

faq.q: Can cold medication cause a positive methamphetamine result?
faq.a: Some sympathomimetics can cross-react; confirm positives by GC-MS/LC-MS.

morphine.name: Morphine
morphine.what: Morphine is a naturally occurring opiate analgesic; also a metabolite of heroin and codeine.
morphine.significance: Morphine screening detects opiate use and heroin/codeine exposure.
morphine.limitations: May reflect prescription opiates; confirm to identify source.

opiates.name: Opiates (Class)
opiates.what: Opiates are a class of naturally derived narcotic analgesics (morphine, codeine, heroin metabolites).
opiates.significance: Class-level screening flags opiate exposure; lab confirmation identifies the specific opiate.
opiates.limitations: Does not detect synthetic opioids (fentanyl, oxycodone); confirm positives.

benzodiazepines.name: Benzodiazepines
benzodiazepines.what: Benzodiazepines are sedative-hypnotic medications (e.g., diazepam, alprazolam) with misuse potential.
benzodiazepines.significance: Screened in workplace and clinical toxicology; cross-reactivity varies by specific benzo.
benzodiazepines.limitations: Cross-reactivity varies by benzodiazepine; confirm positives.

fentanyl.name: Fentanyl
fentanyl.what: Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid driving the current opioid crisis.
fentanyl.significance: Fentanyl screening is critical due to its potency and prevalence as an adulterant.
fentanyl.interpretation: Positive = fentanyl detected (presumptive). Negative = below cut-off.
fentanyl.limitations: Does not detect all fentanyl analogs; confirm positives by LC-MS/MS.

faq.q: Does a fentanyl test detect all analogs?
faq.a: No — some analogs are not detected; confirm positives by LC-MS/MS.

references: SAMHSA. Drug testing guidelines; confirmatory LC-MS/MS per CLIA standards.

ketamine.name: Ketamine
ketamine.what: Ketamine is a dissociative anesthetic with misuse potential.
ketamine.significance: Screened in clinical and workplace settings; cut-off 1000 ng/mL.

methadone.name: Methadone
methadone.what: Methadone is a long-acting opioid used in opioid-substitution therapy (also tested to confirm compliance).
methadone.significance: Screened both to detect misuse and to confirm adherence in treatment programs.
methadone.limitations: Detects methadone (not EDDP metabolite); confirm for compliance monitoring.

xylazine.name: Xylazine
xylazine.what: Xylazine is a veterinary sedative that has emerged as an adulterant in the illicit opioid supply.
xylazine.significance: Xylazine testing is increasingly relevant in toxicology due to its role in overdose cases.
xylazine.limitations: Emerging adulterant — confirm by LC-MS/MS; limited cross-reactivity data.
